data.affected_functions: Core processing, online and mobile banking, bill pay, card authorizations
data.description: Our core processing provider reported a ransomware attack on the environment that hosts our core. Core, online banking and card authorizations were unavailable.
data.title: Core processing provider ransomware

data.summary: Provider called the on-call line: ransomware in its hosting environment; our instance affected.

data.text: Incident response plan activated. IR retainer firm and cyber insurer notified.

cyber_incident.rationale: Ransomware encrypted the core processing environment our provider hosts for us. Member account data and core availability were actually jeopardized without lawful authority.

good_faith_exclusion.rationale: No testing or other authorized activity was under way. The provider confirmed a criminal intrusion.

prong_a.rationale: Vital member services (online banking, bill pay, shared branching) were disrupted. Exposure of member data is still being investigated.

prong_b.rationale: The disruption resulted from a cyberattack (ransomware).

prong_c.rationale: The disruption was caused by a compromise of our third-party core processing and data hosting provider.

substantial.rationale: Core, online banking and card authorizations were unavailable for more than four hours. NCUA's Appendix A lists ransomware on critical systems as an example that likely qualifies.

data.explanation: A substantial cyber incident that meets Prongs A, B and C.

data.basis: Provider confirmed our instance was encrypted; members unable to log in.

data.reference: Voicemail left at 1-833-CYBERCU with name, charter, contact and basic description

data.text: Provider restored core from clean backups. Services back for members.

data.reason: Services restored. Data exposure review continues under the IR firm; member notice decision tracked separately.
